title: Family Law Amendment (Review of Government Support for Single Parents) Bill 2018
short_title: Family Law Amendment (Review of Government Support for Single Parents) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require the Australian Institute of Family Studies to review government support for single parents and examine poverty in their households.
The review would examine the 2013 transfer of certain parents from Parenting Payment to Newstart when their youngest child reached eight, alongside payment adequacy.
The bill would amend the Family Law Act 1975, begin on Royal Assent and require the review's findings to be reported to Parliament.
changes: Conducting the review would become an additional statutory function of the Australian Institute of Family Studies.
The Institute's Director would have six months after commencement to give the Minister a written report.
The Minister would have to table the report in both parliamentary Houses within 15 sitting days of receiving it.
summary.affected: Single parents, the Australian Institute of Family Studies and the Minister administering the Family Law Act would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Wilkie
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the 2012 Gillard government decision to move single parents from parenting payment ($683.50 per fortnight) to Newstart ($537.80 per fortnight) when their youngest child turned eight was a mistake causing widespread hardship, and introduced the Family Law Amendment (Review of Government Support for Single Parents) Bill 2018, which would require the Australian Institute of Family Studies to conduct a six-month review of the cuts' impact, poverty rates among single-parent households, and ways to improve support.
